STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.speaker: Some early authorities
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.claim: Some early authorities considered certain verses, possibly those listed, to have been revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.anchor: Some early authorities, however, considered certain verses, perhaps vv. 20, 23, 91, 93, 114, 141, and 151–53, to have been revealed in Madinah

BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.claim: These three verses contain ten comprehensive duties, unchanged across revealed books, peoples, and eras; whoever practices them enters Paradise, while whoever abandons them enters Hell.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.anchor: هذه الآيات الثلاث إلى قوله : {لعلكم تتقون} تشتمل على عشر خصال جامعة للخير كله لم ينسخهن شيء

BURSEVI:v3p92/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92/r2.claim: The causal phrase means: because of what this surah has stated about divine unity, prophethood, and religious law.
BURSEVI:v3p92/r2.anchor: {وأن} بتقدير اللام علة للفعل المؤخر أي ولأن {هاذآ} أي : ما ذكر في هذه السورة

BURSEVI:v3p92/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92/r3.claim: The Prophet’s “path” is his way and law, called a path because it leads to Paradise; its attribution is by following it, not by originating it.
BURSEVI:v3p92/r3.anchor: {صراطي} أي : مسلكي وشريعتي ، وسمي الشرع طريقا لأنه يؤدي إلى الثواب في الجنة

BURSEVI:v3p92/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92/r4.claim: The straight path is firmly right; the other paths include Judaism, Christianity, and other religions.
BURSEVI:v3p92/r4.anchor:
{مستقيما} حال مؤكدة ، أي مستويا قويما.
{فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل} أي : الطريق المختلفة

BURSEVI:v3p92/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92/r5.claim: The grammar after the prohibition suppresses one of two successive tāʾs, and the causative bāʾ means the divergent paths separate you.
BURSEVI:v3p92/r5.anchor: {فتفرق بكم} منصوب بإضمار أن بعد الفاء في جواب النهي ، أصله فتتفرق حذفت منه إحدى التاءين

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r1.claim: God’s approved religion is Islam, so the Prophet’s straight path is identical with God’s path.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r1.anchor: {عن سبيله} أي : عن دين الله الذي ارتضى وبه أوصى وهو الإسلام

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r2.claim: This is the tenth duty: follow God’s path and leave every other path to avoid disbelief and error.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r2.anchor:
جزدري مصطفا
{ذالكم} أي : اتباع سبيله وترك اتباع سائر السبل.

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r3.claim: The Prophet drew one line as God’s path and other lines on each side, saying a devil calls people along each side path.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r3.anchor: ولما تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية خط خطا فقال : "هذا سبيل الله"

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r4.claim: The law is a path finer than hair and sharper than a sword; people repeatedly ask for guidance to it, and deviation here means slipping from the afterlife bridge.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r4.anchor: واعلم : أن الشرع ههنا هو الصراط المستقيم وهو أحد من السيف وأدق من الشعر

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r5.speaker: عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says many slip from the bridge, especially women; the author adds that most men of his time follow desires and customs like women.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "الزالون عن الصراط كثير وأكثر من يزل عنه النساء"

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r6.claim: Religion has again become strange, and only a rare person offers true companionship or deserves it.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r6.anchor: والدين بدأ غريبا وعاد غريبا فلا يوجد من يستأنس به ويستأهل له إلا نادرا

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r7.speaker: محققان
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r7.claim: The Persian Tafsir says realized people know that all paths begin from God and end in one; Qunawi describes God’s encompassing reality or knowledge as the traveler’s beginning and end.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r7.anchor: محققان بر آنندكه صراط متعين نكردد الاميان بدايتي ونهايتي وعارف داندكه بدايت همه ازكيست

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r8.speaker: صدر الدين قونوي
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r8.claim: Qunawi’s teaching is that God encompasses all things, whether by existence or knowledge, making all paths turn toward Him.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r8.anchor: حق بهمه اشيا ثابت است والله بكل شيء محيط وآن احاطه وجودى است يا علمي

BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r9.claim: The Persian poem concludes that every step and every road leads through the Beloved’s street.
BURSEVI:v3p92#2/r9.anchor:
هرجا قدمى زديم در كوى توبود
هركوشه كه برفتيم سوى توبود

QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r1.claim: The straight path is the way of virtues, whose source is unity; only those aided by God after annihilation can traverse its balanced middle and subsist through divine attributes.
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r1.anchor: أي: طريق الفضائل لأن منبع الفضيلة هي الوحدة.

QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r2.claim: God's straight path is traversed by one who stands through God without leaning for an ulterior aim; other ways are doctrines and religions made by custom and desire.
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r2.anchor: أي: طريقي لا يسلكها إلا من قام بي مستويا غير مائل إلى اليمين والشمال لغرض

QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet drew the guidance path and side paths with a satan calling from each; he recited this verse. Qashani gives no grading.
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r3.anchor:
وروى ابن مسعود
" عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه خط خطا فقال: " هذا سبيل الرشاد " "

QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153#2/r4.claim: Avoiding divergent paths requires rejecting the demands of whims and the soul and keeping to virtues under God's protection.

SULAMI:v1p217/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p217/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v1p217/r1.claim: The straight way is the heart's road to God through turning away from everything else.
SULAMI:v1p217/r1.anchor: قال جعفر بن محمد : طريق من القلب إلى الله بالإعراض عما سواه

SULAMI:v1p217/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p217/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p217/r2.claim: The straight way is one in which the self has no desire or share.
SULAMI:v1p217/r2.anchor: قال سهل : الطريق المستقيم هو الذي لا يكون للنفس فيه مراد ولا حظ

TUSTARI:6:153/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:153/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:153/r1.claim: The straight path excludes followers of religious innovations and passions, who have no repentance; a reported prophetic saying says God has barred repentance for them.
TUSTARI:6:153/r1.anchor: قال: الطريق المستقيم هو الذي لا يكون لأصحاب الأهواء والبدع في الدين، هم ليست لهم توبة

TUSTARI:6:153/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:153/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:6:153/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says every sin has repentance except innovations and passions; he disowns their followers, and God has narrowed their repentance.
TUSTARI:6:153/r2.anchor:
كما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" لكل ذنب توبة، إلا لأصحاب البدع والأهواء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163#3/r1.claim: The forbidden paths veer away from God's straight path to its right or left; an Arab saying urges staying on the road and avoiding side tracks.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p163#3/r1.anchor: يريد السبل التي تعدل عنه يمينا وشمالا

NAHHAS:v2p106/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r8.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p106/r8.claim: The Medinan, Abu Amr, and Asim reading وأن هذا is estimated by al-Khalil and Sibawayh as وليكون هذا صراطي, with an implied conjunction.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r8.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأبي عمرو وعاصم وتقديرها عند الخليل وسيبويه

NAHHAS:v2p106/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p106/r9.claim: Al-Farra takes وأن هذا as genitive, meaning God enjoined you to follow that this is My straight path.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r9.anchor: والفراء يذهب إلى أنها في موضع خفض بمعنى ذلكم وصاكم به ووصاكم بأن هذا صراطي

NAHHAS:v2p106/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r10.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p106/r10.claim: Al-Kisaʾi takes it as accusative on the same interpretation, with the preposition omitted.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r10.anchor: والكسائي يذهب إلى أنها في موضع نصب على هذا المعنى إلا أنه لما حذف الباء نصب

NAHHAS:v2p106/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r11.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p106/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read وإن هذا with kasra as a new sentence.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي ( وإن هذا ) بكسر الهمزة وهذا مستأنف

NAHHAS:v2p106/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r12.claim: With light hamza, وأن هذا can be nominative as a subject or accusative; the path is straight, with مستقيما circumstantial.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r12.anchor: ومن قرأ ( وأن هذا ) بالتخفيف فهذا عنده في موضع رفع بالابتداء ويجوز النصب

NAHHAS:v2p106/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r13.claim: Following the straight path means avoiding the different religions; فتفرق is the response to the prohibition.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r13.anchor: فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل أي لا تتبعوا الديانات المختلفة ( فتفرق بكم عن سبيله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ، جابر بن عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r1.claim: The Prophet drew a center line with side lines, called the center God's path, and recited the verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فخط خطا ، وخط خطين عن يمينه ، وخط خطين عن يساره ، ثم وضع في الخط الاوسط فقال : هذا سبيل الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r2.claim: The Prophet drew a straight line and branching paths, each with a devil calling to it, then recited this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r2.anchor: عن أبي وائل عن عبد لله بن مسعود قال : خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطا ، ثم خط يمينا وشمالا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ، يقول : لا تتبعوا الضلالات .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r4.claim: The forbidden paths are innovations and doubtful matters.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قوله : ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله قال : البدع والشبهات .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r5.claim: The verse forbids paths other than Islam because they separate people from Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r5.anchor: قال : سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم ، في قوله : ولا تتبعو السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ، قال : نهاهم ان يتبعوا السبل سوى الاسلام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r6.claim: The five daily prayers help people guard against Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1421/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : لعلكم تتقون ، يقول : لعلكم تتقون النار بالصلوات الخمس .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1422/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1422/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1422/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد : لعلكم تتقون ، قال : لعلكم تطيعوه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.claim: The three linked groups are social order opened by avoiding shirk, interpersonal and economic order opened by protecting orphan property, and the comprehensive principle of following Islam's straight path and avoiding deviant paths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.anchor: إلى ثلاثة أقسام : الأول : أحكام بها إصلاح الحالة الاجتماعية العامة بين الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.claim: Each of the three sections is closed with a testament from God, repeated three times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.anchor: وقد ذيل كل قسم من هذه الأقسام بالوصاية به بقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r1.claim: The conjunction links this command to the prohibition of associating partners in 6:151; its concluding exhortations parallel the sequence of purposes and affirm following Quranic revelation to the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r1.anchor: الواو عاطفة على جملة : { ألا تشركوا به شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r2.claim: They read anna with an open hamza and doubled nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وعاصم ، وأبو جعفر : { أن } بفتح الهمزة وتشديد النون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r3.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r3.claim: They attach anna to what the Lord prohibited in 6:151, making it an object of recitation: the Prophet is to recite that this is God's straight path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r3.anchor: وعن الفراء والكسائي أنه معطوف على : { ما حرم ربكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r4.claim: Reporting Sibawayh's grammatical approach, he construes an omitted causal lām before anna: follow the path because it is straight, with the fronted reason functioning almost as a condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r4.anchor: وعن أبي علي الفارسي : أن قياس قول سيبويه أن تحمل ( أن ) ، أي تعلق على قوله : { فاتبعوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r5.claim: They read inna with a closed hamza, preserving the order without ellipsis; following branches from the assertion that the path is straight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف : { وإن } بكسر الهمزة وتشديد النون فلا تحويل في نظم الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r6.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r6.claim: They read anna open with a still nūn, either as a reduced emphatic particle with an implied subject pronoun, or preferably as explanatory and coordinated with the command not to associate partners; the repeated particle marks a change in style.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، ويعقوب : ( وأن ) بفتح الهمزة وسكون النون على أنها مخففة من الثقيلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r1.claim: The straight path points to the whole law brought by Muhammad; al-Tabari says it points specifically to the preceding commandments beginning at 6:151.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r1.anchor: الإشارة هي إلى الشرع الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بجملته، وقال الطبري: الإشارة هي إلى هذه الوصايا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r2.claim: The readings include wa-anna with a heavy nūn, wa-in with kasra, and wa-an with a light nūn; Ibn Masʿud’s codex omits an altogether.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r2.anchor:
قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو
عمرو «وأن هذا» بفتح الهمزة وتشديد النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r3.claim: With fatḥa the clause can mean follow this because it is the straight path, or connect to the earlier prohibition; a light nūn can connect to an lā tushrikū and Sibawayh treats it as a light form of the emphatic particle, while kasra begins a new sentence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r3.anchor: فأما من فتح الألف فالمعنى عنده كأنه قال ولأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud describes God’s road as a straight path beginning with Muhammad’s law and ending in Paradise, from which side paths lead toward Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود إن الله جعل طريقا صراطا مستقيما طرفه محمد عليه السلام وشرعه ونهايته الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r5.claim: The Prophet drew a straight line for God’s path, then side lines with a devil calling on each, and recited this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r5.anchor: وقال أيضا خط لنا الرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما خطا، فقال: هذا سبيل الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r6.claim: The verse warns people of passions, innovations, anomalous legal views, excessive disputation, and theological speculation as sources of error and unsound belief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية تعلم أهل الأهواء والبدع والشذوذ في الفروع وغير ذلك من أهل التعمق في الجدل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r7.claim: The earlier prohibitions are obvious to rational people, hence the appeal to reason; later prohibitions involve desires and call for remembrance, while following the complete path entails virtues and taqwa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363#3/r7.anchor: ومن حيث كانت المحرمات الأول لا يقع فيها عاقل قد نظر بعقله جاءت العبارة لعلكم تعقلون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, and Abu ʿAmr read wa-anna with fatḥa and doubled nūn; al-Farra allows it to depend on “I recite” or on “that is what He enjoined, and that this is My path.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وأن بفتح الألف مع تشديد النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads the particle with fatḥa but a light nūn, treating it as a reduced form of the emphatic particle.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بفتح الألف أيضا إلا أنه خفف النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the particle with kasra and doubled nūn as the start of a new sentence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بتشديد النون مع كسر الألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r4.claim: The straight path is interpreted as either the Qurʾan or Islam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r4.anchor: وفي الصراط قولان أحدهما أنه القرآن والثاني الإسلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the paths are misguidances; Mujahid says innovations and doubts; Muqatil says forbidden livestock and crops.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r5.anchor: السبل فقال ابن عباس هي الضلالات وقال مجاهد البدع والشبهات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p151/r6.claim: Following other paths diverts people from God’s path, meaning His religion.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r1.claim: God commands believers to remain united and forbids disagreement and division in religion; Mujāhid and others say earlier peoples perished through religious disputation and quarrels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r1.anchor: أمر الله المؤمنين بالجماعة، ونهاهم عن الاختلاف والفرقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r2.claim: The Prophet drew one straight line as God's path and side lines as other paths, each with a devil calling to it; al-Ḥākim calls the chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365#2/r2.anchor: هذه السبل ليس منها سبيل إلا عليه شيطان يدعو إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r1.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticates the Ibn Masʿūd report through both routes; Ibn Kathīr suggests ʿĀṣim may have heard it from both Zur and Abū Wāʾil, each from Ibn Masʿūd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r1.anchor: ولعل هذا الحديث عند عاصم بن أبي النجود، عن زر، وعن أبي وائل شقيق بن سلمة كلاهما عن ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r2.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r2.claim: A supporting report depicts the straight path with the Prophet's line and the devil's paths on either side; al-Ḥākim says its route from al-Shaʿbī is not dependable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r2.anchor: وشاهد هذا الحديث حديث الشعبي عن جابر، من وجه غير معتمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r3.claim: The Ibn Masʿūd report is the main authority despite possible consequential variation, and it may also have been transmitted as Ibn Masʿūd's own statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p366/r3.anchor: ولكن العمدة على حديث ابن مسعود، مع ما فيه من الاختلاف إن كان مؤثرا، وقد روي موقوفا عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r1.claim: Asked about the straight path, Ibn Masʿūd describes a route ending in Paradise flanked by side roads with callers; those taking the side roads end in Hell, while the straight route ends in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r1.anchor: تركنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في أدناه، وطرفه في الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r2.speaker: النواس بن سمعان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r2.claim: The Prophet's parable identifies the straight path as Islam, its walls as God's limits, open doors as forbidden things, the caller at its head as God's Book, and the inner caller as God's counsel in each Muslim heart; al-Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367/r2.anchor: فالصراط الإسلام، والسوران حدود الله، والأبواب المفتحة محارم الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r1.claim: God's path is singular because truth is one, while the other paths are plural because they divide and branch; the contrast is like believers being brought from darkness into light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r1.anchor: الحق واحد؛ ولهذا جمع لتفرقها وتشعبها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r2.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r2.claim: The Prophet sought a pledge to uphold the three verses beginning 6:151: fulfillment earns God's reward; violation may be punished in this life or left to God's choice in the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p367#2/r2.anchor: ومن وفى بهن أجره على الله، ومن انتقص منهن شيئا

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r1.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Yaʿqub read وإن with light kasra and silent nūn; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī double the nūn; other readers use أن with fatḥa and doubling.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب وإن هذا بكسر ألف أن وسكون النون

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r2.claim: Readers differ in the vowel of the yāʾ in ṣirāṭī and in saying ṣirāṭī or sirāṭī; these are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r2.anchor: والقراء أجمعوا على سكون الياء من صراطي غير ابن عامر فإنه فتحها

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r3.claim: With fatḥa, the clause can attach to the preceding prohibition or mean ‘because this is My path’; with kasra, it can continue ‘recite’ or begin a new sentence.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r3.anchor: فأما فتح (إن) ففيه وجهان: الأول: العطف على ألا تشركوا.

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r4.claim: Ṣirāṭ means road; religious law is a road to Paradise, whereas Satan's way leads to Hell.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r4.anchor: الصراط: الطريق، وإنما قيل للشرع طريق؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى الجنة

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r5.claim: Accusative mustaqīman highlights that the path is straight as well as a path; it is parsed as a circumstantial phrase or specification.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r5.anchor: إنما الفائدة في اجتماع أنه صراط، وأنه مستقيم

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r6.claim: God's straight path is Islam; another gloss is the Qur'an and proofs, without crookedness or contradiction.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r6.anchor: أي: الإسلام طريقي الذي أمرت بها، وقيل: القرآن وسائر الحجج

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r7.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r7.claim: The forbidden divergent paths are religions opposed to Islam or paths of disbelief; following the true way means practicing and affirming it and observing its lawful and forbidden parts.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r7.anchor: فاتبعوه أي: اقتدوا به واعملوا به، واعتقدوا صحته

JISHUMI:v4p2468/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r8.claim: Leaving the true path divides people and destroys unity; God's charge may refer to the Qur'an, Islam, preceding commands, avoiding sins, or avoiding punishment through obedience.
JISHUMI:v4p2468/r8.anchor: فتفرق بكم عن سبيله يعني إذا تركتم طريق الحق المستقيم تفرقتم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.claim: For the fatha reading of ‘and this is My path,’ supply a purpose lām: follow it because it is straight; the kasra reading gives the same cause, supported by 72:18.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r4.anchor: قلت : أجعل قوله : { وأن هاذا صراطي مستقيما } ( الأنعام : 153 ) علة للاتباع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r1.claim: A light-an reading has an omitted pronoun of the matter; al-Aʿmash reads ‘this is My path,’ while the ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy codices read ‘this is your Lord’s path.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r1.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما ) بتخفيف ( أن ) وأصله : وأنه هذا صراطي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r2.claim: The divergent paths are Judaism, Christianity, Magianism, innovations, and misguidance; they divide people away from Islam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r2.anchor: الطرق المختلفة في الدين ، من اليهودية والنصرانية ، والمجوسية ، وسائر البدع والضلالات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r3.claim: Another reading assimilates the tāʾ in fatafarraqa.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r4.claim: The Prophet drew one line as right guidance and side lines each with a devil calling to it, then recited the verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r4.anchor: وروى أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 383 ) أنه خط خطا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these commandments are established and never abrogated in any scripture.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r6.speaker: وقيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r6.claim: Another report calls them scripture’s foundation: those who follow enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r6.anchor: وقيل : إنهن أم الكتاب ، من عمل بهن دخل الجنة ، ومن تركهن دخل النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r7.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears these commandments were the first thing in the Torah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r7.anchor: وعن كعب الأحبار : والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذه الآيات لأول شيء في التوراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r8.claim: ‘Then We gave Moses the Book’ coordinates with ‘He enjoined you’; the command is ancient and was entrusted to each community through its prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p76/r8.anchor: هذه التوصية قديمة ، لم تزل توصاها كل أمة على لسان نبيهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r16.claim: The straight path is either the Qur'an or the religious law; it is called a path because it leads to Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r16.anchor: أحدهما : القرآن . والثاني : الشرع وسمي ذلك صراطا , والصراط هو الطريق لأنه يؤدي إلى الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r17.claim: Following the straight path means acting according to it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r18.claim: The forbidden paths may be superseded revealed books, superseded former religions, or innovations and doubtful doctrines.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r18.anchor: ما تقدم من الكتب المنزلة نسخها بالقرآن , وهو محتمل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r19.claim: Being divided from God's path may mean leaving His religion, or breaking unity in supporting religion and fighting its enemies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r19.anchor: أن يكون سبيله نصرة دينه وجهاد أعدائه

MUQATIL:6:153-154/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:153-154/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:153-154/r1.claim: The straight path is the upright religion; avoid paths of forbidden error that divide people from God’s way. These ordinances are clear and binding on all Adam’s descendants, never abrogated.
MUQATIL:6:153-154/r1.anchor: فهذه الآيات المحكمات لم ينسخهن شىء من جميع الكتب،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r1.speaker: شامي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r1.claim: The Syrian reading lightens أن, from أنه with an omitted pronoun; this makes the straight path a reason for following it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r1.anchor: و لأن هذا صراطى فهو علة للاتباع بتقدير اللام و أن بالتخفيف شامى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads إن as a new sentence at its beginning.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r2.anchor: أن بالتخفيف شامى وأصله و أنه على أن الهاء ضمير الشأن والحديث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r3.speaker: على
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r3.claim: ʿAlī also reads إن as a new sentence.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r3.anchor: ﴿ مستقيما ﴾ حال ﴿ فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل ﴾ الطرق المختلفة فى الدين من اليهودية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r4.claim: The path is straight, and the commands to follow it and avoid diverging religious paths apply to Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, innovations, and error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r4.anchor: الطرق المختلفة فى الدين من اليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r5.claim: The Prophet drew one straight line as God's path, then six slanting lines on each side, each with a devil calling to it, and recited this verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r5.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خط خطا مستويا ثم قال هذا سبيل الرشد وصراط الله فاتبعوه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r6.claim: Splitting each of the twelve paths into six yields seventy-two divergent routes away from Islam.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r6.anchor: ثم يصير كل واحد من الأثنى عشر طريقا ستة طرق فتكون اثنين وسبعين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these decisive verses in all the scriptures have never been abrogated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r8.speaker: كعب
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r8.claim: Kaʿb says these verses were the first thing in the Torah.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r8.anchor: وعن كعب أن هذه الآيات لأول شيء فى التوارة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r9.claim: The sequence from understanding to remembering and then God-consciousness reflects reasoning, taking heed, and avoiding forbidden acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p353/r9.anchor: ذكر اولا تعقلون ثم تذكرون ثم تتقون لأنهم إذا عقلوا تفكروا ثم تذكروا أى اتعظوا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r15.claim: This great verse links to the preceding commands: after prohibitions and orders, it warns against every other path and orders following God's path.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r15.anchor: فإنه لما نهى وأمر حذر هنا عن اتباع غير سبيله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r16.claim: Al-Farraʾ and al-Kisaʾi parse “wa-an” with an implied “I recite”; al-Farraʾ also allows genitive coordination, while al-Khalil and Sibawayh understand “and because this is My path,” citing 72:18.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r16.anchor: أي وأتل أن هذا صراطي عن الفراء والكسائي

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read “wa-inna” with a kasra as a new sentence: what has just been mentioned is God's straight path.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r1.anchor: على الاستئناف أي الذي ذكر في هذه الآيات

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yaʿqub read the conjunction in its light form; it behaves like the heavy form with an implicit pronoun of the story, may be nominative or accusative, or may be emphatic and extra, as in 12:96.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r2.anchor: إلا أن فيه ضمير القصة والشان أي وأنه هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r3.claim: The straight path is Islam, the Prophet Muhammad's revealed law, and its end is Paradise; following the main road saves, while branching paths lead to Hell, and the phrase about paths means they cause deviation.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r4.claim: In a soundly authenticated report in al-Darimi, Ibn Masʿud says the Prophet drew one line as God's path and side lines as other paths, each with a devil calling people to it, then recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r5.claim: Jabir reports in Ibn Majah a similar lesson: the Prophet drew the center line as God's path, added lines to the right and left, and recited the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the divergent paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, other religions, religious innovations, deviant legal doctrines, and excessive disputation or speculative theology; Qurtubi agrees this is correct.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r6.anchor: ومظنة لسوء المعتقد قاله ابن عطية

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r7.claim: A report cited from al-Tabari pictures the straight path as beginning near the Prophet and ending in Paradise, with side roads that lead to Hell when callers draw people onto them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r7.anchor: قال لابن مسعود: ما الصراط المستقيم؟ قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud urges learning before knowledge disappears with its bearers, warns against hair-splitting, excess, and innovations, and calls people to the ancient way; al-Darimi transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: تعلموا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r9.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r9.claim: Ibn Shihab connects the warning against divergent paths to the warning that people split their religion into sects in 6:159.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:153/r9.anchor: قال ابن شهاب: وهذا كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi urges holding firmly to the straight path and the sound Sunnah followed by the early righteous generations as the route to safety and gain.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's instruction: take what he commands and stop what he forbids.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r3.speaker: العرباض بن سارية
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r3.claim: In a report al-Tirmidhi authenticates in meaning, the Prophet's tearful farewell counsel says his community has a clear way, will face much disagreement, and must cling to his Sunnah and the rightly guided caliphs, reject innovations as misguidance, and obey even an Abyssinian slave.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r4.claim: In a letter about predestination, Umar counsels piety, moderation, the Prophetic Sunnah, abandoning innovations, and staying with the community; he says the first generations had sufficient knowledge and insight, while later people either fell short or went beyond them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r4.anchor: فكتب إليه: أما بعد، فإني أوصيك

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r5.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r5.claim: Sahl al-Tustari urges following transmitted precedent and the Sunnah, warning that soon those who mention the Prophet and imitate him in every state will be censured, shunned, disowned, and humiliated.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r5.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري: عليكم بالاقتداء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r6.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r6.claim: Sahl says innovations spread because Sunnis debated their proponents publicly; had the innovators been left alone, their ideas would have died with them. He adds that Iblis first inspires devotional practice, then innovation, and strips the devotion away when it is proclaimed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#2/r6.anchor: قال سهل: إنما ظهرت البدعة على يدي أهل السنة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r1.speaker: سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r1.claim: Sahl cites a report he calls the strongest about innovators: God bars an innovator from Paradise, so Jews and Christians are more hopeful than such a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r1.anchor: فاليهودي والنصراني أرجى منهم. قال سهل:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r2.speaker: سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r2.claim: Sahl advises one who wants to honor his religion not to visit rulers, be alone with women, or argue with people of sectarian desires; he says to follow rather than innovate because enough has already been provided.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r2.anchor: قال سهل: من أراد أن يكرم دينه فلا يدخل على السلطان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r3.claim: Al-Darimi reports that Ibn Masʿud rejected a group counting repeated formulae of remembrance with pebbles in circles, telling them to count sins instead; he warned that good intentions do not guarantee a good act and called their practice an opening to misguidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r3.anchor: إلى عبد الله بن مسعود فقال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r4.claim: Asked about sectarian innovators, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz tells a man to hold to the religion of the Bedouins and the child at school, leaving other paths aside.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r4.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز وسأله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r5.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r5.claim: Al-Awzaʿi recounts Iblis asking his followers how they reach Adam's children; they say through every route but repentance, so he vows to spread sectarian desires that people will not seek forgiveness for.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r6.claim: Mujahid says he does not know which is the greater blessing: being guided to Islam or being protected from sectarian desires.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ولا أدري أي النعمتين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r7.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi explains that the people of desires are so called because they plunge into the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r7.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إنما سموا أصحاب الأهواء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r8.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r8.claim: Sahl rules against praying behind, marrying, or marrying into the Muʿtazila, calling them unbelievers for denying created Paradise and Hell, the bridge, intercession, punishment and angels of the grave, vision of God, and other doctrines while anathematizing believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r8.anchor: وسئل سهل بن عبد الله عن الصلاة خلف المعتزلة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r9.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r9.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad says that loving an innovator nullifies one's deeds and removes Islam's light from the heart; Qurtubi notes that he cited this earlier with more detail.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r9.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: من أحب صاحب بدعة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r10.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r10.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says innovation is dearer to Iblis than sin because sin can be repented from whereas innovation is not repented from.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#3/r10.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: البدعة أحب إلى إبليس

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls it worship to look at a Sunnah-following person who invites others to the Sunnah and forbids innovations.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: النظر إلى الرجل من أهل السنة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r2.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya urges adherence to the original practice before people split; Hasan al-Basri, hearing this from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, affirms that it is sincere and true advice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r2.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: عليكم بالأمر الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r3.claim: Qurtubi notes that the warning about Israel's seventy-two sects and this community's seventy-three was discussed earlier in Aal ʿImran.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r3.anchor: وقد مضى في «آل عمران» معنى قوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r4.claim: Some learned authorities say the extra sect in Muhammad's community consists of people who oppose scholars and hate jurists, something unknown among earlier peoples.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r4.anchor: قال بعض العلماء العارفين: هذه الفرقة التي زادت

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r5.speaker: رافع بن خديج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r5.claim: Rafiʿ ibn Khadij reports the Prophet warning of people who unknowingly deny God and the Quran by accepting part and rejecting part, making Iblis equal to God in creation, power, and provision, and provoking enmity and argument; he calls them the community's heretics.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r5.anchor: روى رافع بن خديج أنه سمع رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r6.claim: Qurtubi links the ban on following divergent paths to the prohibition on sitting with people who dispute God's signs, citing 6:68; 4:140 later says those who sit with them share their ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r6.anchor: هذه السورة النهي عن مجالسة أهل البدع والأهواء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r7.claim: A group of imams, including Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Awzaʿi, and Ibn al-Mubarak, say a persistent companion of innovators is treated as one of them; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz applied the same principle to people sitting with wine drinkers.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#4/r7.anchor: وقد ذهب إلى هذا جماعة من أئمة هذه الأمة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#5/r1.claim: When told he merely sat with innovators to dispute them, the response was that he must stop, and if he refuses he is joined to them in judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151-153#5/r1.anchor: قيل له: فإنه يقول إني أجالسهم

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the opening with wa-an and a light nūn; the underlying form is wa-annahu, with hāʾ as the pronoun of the matter.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { تذكرون وأن هاذا } بفتح الألف وسكون النون وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { وأن } بكسر الألف وتشديد النون أما قراءة ابن عامر فأصلها { وأنه * هاذا صراطي }

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r2.speaker: الأعشى
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line illustrates the ellipsis of the pronoun of the matter in the construction Ibn ʿĀmir reads.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r2.anchor: قال الأعشى : في فتية كسيوف الهند قد علموا … أن هالك كل من يحفى وينتعل

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r3.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read inna with kasra, either as the Prophet saying, after reciting the prohibition, that this is his path, or as a new sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r3.anchor: وأما كسر { ءان } فالتقدير { أتل ما حرم } ( الأنعام : 151 ) وأتل { إن هذا * صراطي } بمعنى أقول وقيل على الاستئناف .

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the open reading as an object of recitation, or as genitive after God's preceding command to the community.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r4.anchor: وأما فتح أن فقال الفراء فتح { ءان } من وقوع أتل عليها يعني وأتل عليكم { إن هذا * صراطي مستقيما }

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r5.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r5.claim: Sībawayh parses the open reading causally: follow this path because it is straight, like the construction in 23:52; he gives the same rationale for 72:18.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r5.anchor: من فتح { ءان } فقياس قول سيبويه أنه حملها على قوله : { فاتبعوه } والتقدير لأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone opens the yāʾ in ṣirāṭī; Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read the word with sīn, Ḥamza between ṣād and zāy, and the rest with clear ṣād.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r6.anchor: القراء أجمعوا على سكون الياء من { صراطي } غير ابن عامر فإنه فتحها وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر { * سراطي } بالسين وحمزة بين الصاد

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r7.speaker: الأعمش
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads wa-hādhā ṣirāṭī; the codices of ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy instead read “the path of your Lord.”
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرأ الأعمش { وهاذا * صراطي } وفي مصحف عبد الله { وهاذا صراط * ربكم }

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r8.claim: The path summarizes the two preceding verses, all the Prophet's teaching of Islam, and the whole straight religion; follow it in general and detail without deviating into error.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r8.anchor: دخل فيه كل ما بينه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من دين الإسلام وهو المنهج القويم والصراط المستقيم

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Prophet drew one straight line as the path of guidance, then side lines with a devil calling from each, and recited this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r9.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه خط خطا ، ثم قال : هذا سبيل الرشد ثم خط عن يمينه وعن شماله خطوطا

RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these decisive commands were never abrogated in any revealed book: whoever practices them enters Paradise and whoever abandons them enters Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v14p3/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r7.claim: For the open reading of أن, he explains the clause as the reason for following the straight path, with an omitted causal lām; the kasra reading supports that sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:153/r7.anchor:
أجعل قوله " وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما " علة للاتباع بتقدير اللام كقوله
وأن المساجد لله

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r1.claim: The two Kufan readers read إن with kasra as a new sentence coordinated with the preceding sentence; it explains why the path should be followed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان بكسر " إن " على الاستئناف و " فاتبعوه " جملة معطوفة على الجملة قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r2.claim: The kasra reading makes the clause a reason for following the path, and the author says the following fa is analyzed as in the other reading.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r2.anchor: وهذه الجملة الاتئنافية تفيد التعليل لقوله " فاتبعوه "

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads أن with an open hamza and a light n; the other readers open the hamza with a doubled n.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر " وأن " بفتح الهمزة وتخفيف النون، والباقون بالفتح أيضا والتشديد

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r4.claim: For the doubled reading, he coordinates the clause as the object of أتل: I recite to you that this is my straight path.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r4.anchor: أحدها: وهو الظاهر أنها في محل نصب نسقا على ما حرم أي: أتل ما حرم وأتل أن هذا صراطي

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r5.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r5.claim: He makes أن and its clause coordinate with أن لا تشركوا as a substitute for ما حرم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنها منصوبة المحل أيضا نسقا على " أن لا تشركوا " إذا قلنا بأن " أن " المصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r6.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r6.claim: He derives the open reading from an omitted causal lām: because this is the straight path, follow it, citing parallel Sibawayh analyses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r6.anchor: الثالث: أنها على إسقاط لام العلة أي: ولأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r7.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r7.claim: He says Sibawayh's analysis makes fa extra as in زيد فقائم; the author notes Sibawayh does not allow that fa in this predicate construction.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r7.anchor: قال الفارسي: " قياس قول سيبويه في فتح الهمزة أن تكون الفاء زائدة كهي في " زيد فقائم

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r8.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r8.claim: He also allows the clause in the genitive, coordinated with the pronoun in به, with the preposition understood.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r8.anchor: الرابع: أنها في محل جر نسقا على الضمير المجرور في " به " أي: ذلكم وصاكم به وبأن هذا

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r9.claim: He objects to coordination with a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition and says it would wrongly mean God commanded the path to be straight.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r9.anchor: ورده أبو البقاء بوجهين أحدهما: العطف على الضمير المجرور من غير إعادة الجار

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r10.claim: The author answers that the preposition is understood after أن because its clause is long and that commanding the path's straightness means avoiding departure from it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#4/r10.anchor: والوجهان مردودان، أما الأول فليس هذا من باب العطف على المضمر من غير إعادة الجار

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r1.claim: Ibn Amir's light-n reading is softened إن with a pronoun of affair, as in the cited verse and poetic line; it admits the same four analyses as the doubled reading.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r1.anchor: وأما قراءة ابن عامر فقالوا: " أن " فيها مخففة من الثقيلة، واسمها ضمير الأمر والشأن

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r2.claim: مستقيما is circumstantial, governed either by ها of attention or by the demonstrative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r2.anchor: و " مستقيما " حال، العامل: إما " ها " التنبيه، وإما اسم الإشارة

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r3.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r3.claim: The Abdullah codex and al-Amash reading omit أن and read وهذا صراطي, supporting the independent-sentence reading with kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله " وهذا صراطي " بدون " أن " وهي قراءة الأعمش، وبها تتأيد قراءة الكسر

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r4.claim: فتفرق is subjunctive after an implicit أن answering the prohibition; the majority lighten its ت while al-Bazzi doubles it by deleting or assimilating a ت.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r4.anchor: فتفرق } منصوب بإضمار " أن " بعد الفاء في جواب النهي والجمهور على " فتفرق " بتاء خفيفة

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r5.claim: بكم can function semantically as an object, meaning the paths divide you, or as a circumstantial phrase meaning you are with them.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r5.anchor: و " بكم " يجوز أن تكون مفعولا به في المعنى أي: فيفرقكم، ويجوز أن تكون حالا

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r6.claim: The ending with piety is apt because following the path protects a person from the Fire.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#5/r6.anchor: وختم هذه بالتقوى وهي اتقاء النار لمناسبة الأمر باتباع الصراط

STUDYQURAN:6:153/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r1.claim: The straight path is the path leading to God and salvation.
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r1.anchor: that leads to God and salvation (see 1:6c)

STUDYQURAN:6:153/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r2.claim: Most commentators identify the path specifically with Islam as taught through Muhammad's guidance and injunctions, including Quranic revelation and the Prophet's Sunnah.
STUDYQURAN:6:153/r2.anchor: for most commentators it was understood to refer specifically to the religious path of Islam, defined by the guidance and injunctions brought by the Prophet Muhammad

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r6.claim: The opening word is read with a fathah and doubled or light n, or with a kasrah; Tabataba'i connects the first forms grammatically to the earlier prohibition and takes the kasrah as a new sentence.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r6.anchor: قرئ { وأن } بفتح الهمزة وتشديد النون وتخفيفها وكأنه بالعطف على موضع

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r7.claim: The straight-path declaration is a lead-in to the prohibition against following divisive paths and straying from God's way.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r7.anchor: فالمراد بالآية أن لا تتفرقوا عن سبيله ولا تختلفوا فيه

TABATABAI:6:153/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153/r1.claim: The declaration parallels the command given to earlier prophets to establish one religion and avoid division; repeating the core religion prepares for the warning against splitting.
TABATABAI:6:153/r1.anchor: فالأمر في الآية بإقامة الدين هو ما وصى من الدين المشروع

TABATABAI:6:153/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153/r2.claim: Tabataba'i reads my path as the Prophet's path, since Muhammad is the speaker delivering these commands; this attribution is consistent with the Qur'an's calling the way of the rightly guided servants the straight path.
TABATABAI:6:153/r2.anchor: ومقتضى ظاهر السياق أن يكون المراد بقوله { صراطي } صراط النبي

TABATABAI:6:153/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153/r3.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:6:153/r3.claim: Most commentators instead take the first-person possessive in my path as God's and identify a shift of person in the passage.
TABATABAI:6:153/r3.anchor: لكن المفسرين كأنهم تسلموا أن ضمير التكلم في قوله { صراطي } لله سبحانه

TABATABAI:6:153/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153/r4.claim: Tabataba'i says the shift is not in my path but in from His path, which can follow the Prophet's quotation of God's command or a divine instruction to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:6:153/r4.anchor: فالالتفات - كما مر - إنما هو في قوله { عن سبيله }

TABATABAI:6:153/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153/r5.claim: God's straight path is the coherent religion grounded in human nature; unlike desire-driven routes, it has no internal contradiction or division among those who follow it.
TABATABAI:6:153/r5.anchor: بخلاف سبيل الله المبني على الفطرة والخلقة ولا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم

TABATABAI:6:151-157/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r3.claim: The third verse forbids religious division because avoiding divergent paths is necessary for piety, which grows through understanding prohibitions, remembering them, and keeping to human nature.
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r3.anchor: والغرض المسوق له الآية الثالثة هو النهي عن التفرق والاختلاف في الدين

TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r1.claim: God promises those who are mindful an exit and a criterion distinguishing truth from falsehood; one remains on the path of piety through reason, recollection, and human nature, while desire and worldly attachment pull one into heedless disobedience.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r1.anchor: إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا

TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r2.claim: Desire-driven paths lack a regulator, so their followers do not stay united; the Qur'an describes many such paths, including those of criminals, corrupters, the ignorant, and people following conjecture and desire.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#2/r2.anchor: والأهواء النفسانية مختلفة لا ضابط يضبطها ولا نظام يحكم عليها

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r1.claim: Piety does not arise through division or by following any available religious route; it is hoped for by adhering to the straight path, as the verse's closing warning makes clear.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r1.anchor: وبالجملة التقوى الديني لا يحصل بالتفرق والاختلاف، والورود في أي مشرعة شرعت

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r2.speaker: القطب الرازي
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r2.claim: Ruh al-Ma'ani says the first ending addresses idolaters' failure to recognize wrongdoing, while the second reminds them of virtues they already practiced.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r2.anchor: لعلهم يذكرون إن عرض لهم نسيان، قاله القطب الرازي. انتهى.

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r3.claim: Tabataba'i says the reported virtues do not match historical accounts of pre-Islamic Arabs, and the explanation confuses Qur'anic recollection with ordinary remembering.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r3.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن الذي ذكره من اتصافهم بحفظ أموال اليتامى وإيفاء الكيل والعدل في القول

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r4.speaker: فخر الرازي
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r4.claim: Fakhr al-Razi says the first five duties are obvious, whereas the four in the second verse are obscure and require much thought to find their proper limits.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r4.anchor: وقال الإمام - يعني الرازي - في التفسير الكبير السبب في ختم كل آية بما ختمت

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r5.claim: Tabataba'i finds Razi's explanation close to his own but says the second duties are not obscure; only calibrating orphan-property care and measures needs care, and the context connects recollection to the duties themselves.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r5.anchor: غير أن الأمور الأربعة المذكورة في الآية الثانية مما يناله الإنسان بأدنى تأمل

TABATABAI:6:153#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan says the third verse ends with piety because following the comprehensive straight path brings eternal rescue and happiness.
TABATABAI:6:153#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو حيان ولما كان الصراط المستقيم هو الجامع للتكاليف

TABATABAI:6:153-154/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:153-154/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:153-154/r1.claim: Tabataba'i replies that Abu Hayyan treats following the straight path as the primary purpose, whereas the context makes it a prelude to forbidding division.
TABATABAI:6:153-154/r1.anchor: وقد تقدم أن مقتضى السياق كونه مقدمة للنهي عن التفرق باتباع السبل الأخرى

TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r5.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet drew a central line as God's straight path, drew side paths with a Satan calling along each, and recited this verse.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم خطا بيده

TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r6.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet drew the central way and two paths on each side, identified the middle as God's path and the sides as Satan's, then recited the verse.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فخط خطا

TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r7.claim: Abu Ja'far says in the Qummi commentary that the divinely guided path is the Imams, and rejecting it means taking other paths and falling into disbelief; Tabataba'i calls this an application of the verse.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#3/r7.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله } قال نحن السبيل فمن أبى فهذه السبل فقد كفر

TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r1.claim: Tabataba'i derives the identification of the path with loyalty to the Prophet's family by combining the command to love kin with the statement that one may seek a path to one's Lord.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r1.anchor: إذا انضم إلى قوله قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ

TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r2.speaker: روايات من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r2.claim: Reports transmitted through both Shi'i and Sunni channels identify Ali as the straight path; Tabataba'i notes that he had discussed them in the first volume's commentary on al-Fatiha.
TABATABAI:6:151-157#4/r2.anchor: وقد وردت عدة روايات من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة أن عليا هو الصراط المستقيم

TABRISI:6:152-153/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153/r2.claim: Most readers open the hamza in wa-anna hādhā; Kufans other than ʿĀṣim read it with kasra. All double its nūn except Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb, who lighten it; Ibn ʿĀmir opens the yāʾ in ṣirāṭī, and Ibn ʿĀmir and Ibn Kathīr read sirāṭ with sīn, while Ḥamza uses an intermediate sound.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكرفة غير عاصم وإن هذا بكسر الهمزة والباقون بفتحها وكلهم شدد النون

TABRISI:6:152-153/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153/r3.claim: Opening wa-anna links the path clause to “follow it,” on a construction like 2:19; with kasra it starts a new sentence. The light form of inna has an understood pronoun of the matter and ṣirāṭī as its predicate.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r3.anchor: وأما من فتح وإن هذا فإنه حملها على فاتبعوه على قياس قول سيبويه

TABRISI:6:152-153/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153/r4.claim: The light and doubled forms of tadhakkarūn are close in meaning and derive from tatadhakkarūn; the source explains deletion versus assimilation of tāʾ.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r4.anchor: القراءتان في تذكرون متقاربتان والأصل تتذكرون فمن خفف حذف التاء الأولى

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “this is My straight path” as the religion of Abrahamic monotheism, the upright and best religion; the listed commands lead to reward and Paradise.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أن هذا ديني دين الحنيفية أقوم الأديان وأحسنها

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid identifies the forbidden divergent paths as disbelief, innovations, and doubtful doctrines.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r9.anchor: ولا تتبعوا السبل } أي طرق الكفر والبدع والشبهات عن مجاهد

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r1.claim: Following divergent paths scatters people away from the religion God chose and enjoined.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r1.anchor: أي فتشتت وتميل وتخالف بكم عن دينه الذي ارتضى وبه أوصى

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the divergent paths as Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and idol worship; they divert people from God’s chosen religion.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: يريد اليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية وعبادة الأوثان عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r3.claim: The verb fattafarraqa is originally fatatafarraqa; following divergent ways scatters people away from God’s path, the religion He chose and enjoined, and the commands are meant to guard against His punishment.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r3.anchor: وأصله فتتفرق { بكم عن سبيله } أي فتشتت وتميل وتخالف بكم عن دينه

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls these rulings clear, un-abrogated prohibitions in all scriptures and universal commands for humanity: those who act on them enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears that these commands are the Torah’s first instruction, beginning with “Say: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden.”
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

THALABI:v4p204/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p204/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says these clear commands were never abrogated, apply to all humanity, form the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise.
THALABI:v4p204/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء في جميع الكتب

THALABI:v4p204/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p204/r9.claim: The straight path is God’s upright religion; the other paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, innovations, and misguidance that scatter people from the Prophet’s way.
THALABI:v4p204/r9.anchor: في هاتين الآيتين صراطي طريقي وديني مستقيما مستويا قويما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n154/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n154/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n154/r1.claim: The phrase means literally “to become scattered.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r1.claim: With fatḥa, anna is governed by atlu; alternatively it may be genitive after the command “that is what He enjoined,” as a coordinated item.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r2.speaker: أبو علي عن سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r2.claim: The fatḥa can be governed by “follow it”: because this is My straight path, follow it, paralleling 23:52 and 72:18.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads anna with an open, light hamza; it carries an implicit pronoun of the matter, like al-Aʿshā’s poetic example meaning “he is doomed.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر (¬3): (وأن هذا) مفتوحة مخففة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r4.claim: With kasra, in begins a new sentence and the fāʾ coordinates it; on the first analysis the fāʾ is extra, and the case of mustaqīman was explained at 6:126.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r5.claim: The straight path is the religion of the ḥanīf, the most upright and best of religions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r5.anchor: يريد: ديني دين الحنيفية أقوم الأديان وأحسنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p534/r6.claim: The commands and prohibitions just given are the straight path that people must follow.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r1.claim: The forbidden side paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and idol worship.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r2.claim: The image is of a traveler leaving the main road for branching paths.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r2.anchor: مثل الذي يسلك الطريق فيأخذ بنيات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r3.claim: The side paths are innovations and doubtful matters.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r4.claim: The paths are misguidance, including forbidding livestock and crops to oneself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r4.anchor: يعني: طريق الضلالة فيما حرموا على

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r5.speaker: ابن عباس؛ مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r5.claim: The paths make people stray from God’s religion; Mujāhid glosses the result as deviation and opposition, and says the command is in the Book to guard against those paths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r6.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r6.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqūn means “so that you may fear.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r7.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r7.claim: These rulings are decisive, abrogated by nothing in any scripture, forbidden to humanity; those who act on them enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p536/r7.anchor: هذه الآيات محكمات، لم ينسخهن شيء في جميع الكتب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r1.claim: The straight path is the religion of upright monotheism, the most upright religion; divergent paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and idol worship.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:153/r2.claim: Divergent paths mislead from God’s religion; God commanded this in scripture so people would guard themselves from them.

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r12.claim: The prior tawhid and these ten commands and prohibitions together form God's straight path, the foundation and method of religion, which people must follow.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r12.anchor: bu ahkâm-ı aşere Benim müstakīm olarak sırâtımdır; doğrudan doğru tuttuğum yolum, caddem, esâs-ı dinim ve minhâcımdır

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r13.claim: People must avoid the many divergent religions, sects, innovations, and errors that split them away from God's path.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r13.anchor: muhtelif dinler, mezhebler, bid‘at ü dalâlet olan türlü türlü yollar arkasında dolaşmayınız

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r14.speaker: İbn Mes‘ud
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r14.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud reports that the Prophet drew one straight line as the guidance path, then lines to its sides, each with a devil calling people, and recited these verses.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r14.anchor: İbn Mes‘ud hazretleri demiştir ki: “Resûlullah bize bir hatt-ı müstakīm çizdi, ‘bu rüşd yoludur’ dedi

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r15.claim: Although paths are popularly said to equal the breaths of creatures, the divinely revealed path that leads to God is one, unifying rather than fragmenting its followers; truth is one and falsehood many.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r15.anchor: yani o kadar çoktur denilmiş. Fakat bütün bunların içinde hakikaten Allah yolu

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r16.claim: A true ruling may differ across times or places, but truth is singular in each case; yesterday's truth need not govern forever, nor must East and West share a ruling.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r16.anchor: Dün hak olan her zaman için hak olmak lâzım gelmez. Garbdaki bir kimse için hak olanın şarktaki için de hak olması iktizâ etmez

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r17.claim: Some fundamental rulings remain unchanged and unabrogated across revealed religions and scriptures; the ten rulings just explained belong to this class.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r17.anchor: bütün dinler bu noktada ittifak eder

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r18.claim: This guidance binds the Prophet too: his enduring practice is God's path, so people find that path by following him and affirming tawhid; fulfilling God's covenant is thereby enacted.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r18.anchor: Peygamber’in doğrudan doğru tuttuğu yoldur. Ve Peygamber’in tuttuğu yol Allah yoludur

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r19.claim: Those who violate the listed duties or follow other paths depart from tawhid, split into factions, and become ruined.

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r20.claim: Unity under tawhid and prophetic guidance is a divine strength; alliances in falsehood are short-lived, while lasting strength comes from seeking unity upon truth.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r20.anchor: Hakīkī kuvvet hakta ittifaktır. Bu da Peygamber’e ittibâ‘etmek ve bu esaslara tutunup dâima cihet-i vahdet taharrî eylemekle olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.claim: After criticizing baseless polytheist rules, these verses set out nine principal divine commands on monotheism and morality, then command following God's straight path as the encompassing duty; the invitation frames these as the sole correct and obligatory way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.anchor: bu âyetlerde asıl benimsenmesi gereken başlıca ilâhî kurallar ve hükümler yer almakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r18.claim: The straight-path command encompasses all previous commands and prohibitions; other paths are ways of thinking and living contrary to Islam that lead people away from God's path and true religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r18.anchor: 153. âyetin bu kısmı yukarıdaki bütün emir ve yasakları kapsamakta
