ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.claim: Verses 155–165 present the Qur’an’s conclusive communication; a prophet cannot produce a demanded sign, and the Prophet declares his guidance through Abraham’s religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.anchor: A prophet does not have the authority to show such a sign.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.claim: The passage invites anyone who wishes to follow the straight path, permits others to wander, and makes each person responsible before God for their deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p6/r.anchor: Everyone is responsible before God for his deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.claim: The basic teachings of Abraham's religion call Quraysh to the straight path; Moses' law likewise guides its adherents to that path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.anchor: the Quraysh too are invited to this straight path. They must not deviate from them and wander in misguidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.claim: These verses detail Abraham's religion and expose the Quraysh's neglect of its duties to God and creatures while claiming adherence through invented food taboos; their first violation is polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.anchor: These verses state the real religion of Abraham (sws) in detail.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: The sequence moves from reflection that frees one from blind following, to recalling truths of human nature, then to taqwā; Sharīʿah's fundamentals emerge from human nature when people heed God's reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: The sharī‘ah is a treasury that has been extracted from our nature and has been consigned to us

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: Grammatically, mustaqīman is an accusative of state governed by the verb in the demonstrative expression.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: is an accusative of state. The verb found in the demonstrative noun is acting on it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: The straight path presented by the Prophet is God's instruction and Abraham's teaching; abandoning other paths prevents deviation and punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: the straight path which the Prophet (sws) is presenting before them should be followed by them; it is instructed by God and taught by Abraham (sws) to his progeny.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: Just as wholesome purity distinguishes lawful food, justice, goodness, and good conventions distinguish commanded conduct from rebellion, lewdness, and vice in Abraham's and Islam's religions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: all things that are enjoined stem from justice, goodness and good conventions and all things that are forbidden stem from rebelliousness, lewdness and vice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p157.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p157.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p157.claim: The straight path of Abraham was given to both Israelite and Ishmaelite descendants; later innovations led to polytheism among Ishmaelites and Judaism or Christianity among Israelites, until Muhammad restored the original path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p157.anchor: the Almighty once again had it recovered through the last Prophet – Muḥammad (sws).

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r1.claim: These readers open أن, geminate nūn, and leave the yāʾ of صراطي silent; Ibn Amir opens أن without gemination and vocalizes the yāʾ, while Hamza and Kisai read وإن with kasra and gemination.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير، ونافع، وعاصم، وأبو عمرو، وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما، مفتوحة الألف مشددة النون، صراطي ساكنة الياء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read سراطي with sīn; Hamza uses an intermediate sound between ṣād and zāy, while the remaining readers use ṣād.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر: سراطي بالسين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r3.claim: Opening أن links the path clause to an implied لِـ: because this is God's straight path, follow it; Sibawayh uses analogous implied prepositions in other verses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r3.anchor: فكذلك لأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r4.claim: With light nūn, أن has a story pronoun and this path is its subject, with صراطي as predicate; kasra instead begins a new sentence and makes the following fa coordinate clauses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p435/r4.anchor: ومن كسر إن* استأنف بها، والفاء في قوله فاتبعوه على قوله عاطفة جملة على جملة، وعلى القول الأول زيادة.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r2.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، عاصم، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r2.claim: In وأن هذا صراطي, the readers vary the initial hamza, nūn doubling, and yāʾ vowel: Ibn Amir opens the yāʾ without doubling nūn, while Hamza and al-Kisai use kasra on the hamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ﴿ وأن هذا ﴾ مفتوحة الألف موقوفة النون / صرطى / مفتوحة الياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r3.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن عامر، حمزة، الباقون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r3.claim: For صراطي, Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read sīn, Hamza uses an intermediate ṣād-zāy sound with variant reports, and the others read ṣād.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر / سراطى / بالسين

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#1/r1.claim: Inna with kasra makes an independent emphatic assertion, rather than the subordinate clause anna; Hamza and al-Kisai read this form.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#1/r1.anchor: Inna (with kasra) instead of anna (with fatḥa) — changes from subordinate clause

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#2/r1.claim: The light an with quiescent nūn is a masdariyya particle rather than emphatic inna, changing syntactic weight but not the core sense.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:2#2/r1.anchor: Light an (with sukūn on nūn) instead of anna (with shadda) — masdariyya particle

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#1/r1.claim: Ibn Amir opens the possessive yāʾ in ṣirāṭiya instead of leaving it quiescent; the fuller pronunciation does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#1/r1.anchor: Fat-ḥa on the yāʾ (ṣirāṭiya) instead of sukūn (ṣirāṭī) — fuller pronunciation

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#2/r1.claim: Qunbul from Ibn Kathir reads sīn instead of ṣād in sirāṭī, a phonological substitution for the same root.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#2/r1.anchor: Sīn replaces ṣād — phonological variant (ibdāl); Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#3/r1.claim: Khalaf from Hamza gives ṣād an intermediate pronunciation with ishmām of zāy.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:4#3/r1.anchor: Ṣād with ishmām of zāy — intermediate pronunciation between ṣ and z

QIRAAT-ER:6:153:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:13#1/r1.claim: The tāʾ assimilates into the following tāʾ in fa-ttafarraqa; this is articulatory and does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:6:153:13#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of tāʾ — phonological variant with tāʾ assimilated into the following tāʾ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p223#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p223#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p223#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud pictures the straight path as the route Muhammad left them, leading to Paradise, while side roads have callers who divert travelers and end in Hell.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p223#2/r1.anchor: أن رجلا سأل ابن مسعود ما الصراط قال تركنا محمد في أدناه وطرفه في الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r1.speaker: الأخوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r1.claim: The two Kufan readers begin a new sentence with kasra on inna and a doubled nūn; the following command coordinates with it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وأن هذا بكسر الهمزة وتشديد النون على الاستئناف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r2.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa; Ibn ʿAmir lightens the nūn while the others double it, and Ibn Abi Ishaq reads wa-in.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتحها وخفف ابن عامر النون وشددها الباقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r3.claim: With a light nūn, the name of inna is omitted as the pronoun of the matter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r3.anchor: فعلى أنه حذف اسم إن وهو ضمير الشأن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r4.claim: One analysis treats the opening particle as causal, with an omitted lām: because this is the straight path, follow it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p690/r4.anchor: أن يكون تعليلا حذف منها اللام تقديره ولأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r1.speaker: الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r1.claim: Al-Farisi says that under Sibawayh's account of the fatḥa, the following faʾ must be an extra particle, as in Zayd fa-qāma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r1.anchor: قياس قول سيبويه في فتح الهمزة أن تكون الفاء زائدة بمنزلتها في زيد فقام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r2.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi coordinates this clause with lā tushrikū if an there is nominalizing; Abu al-Baqaʾ instead coordinates it with mā ḥarrama or the recitation command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r2.anchor: أن تكون معطوفة على ألا تشركوا أي أتل عليكم نفي الإشراك والتوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r3.claim: On Abu al-Baqaʾ's analysis, the path belongs to the speaker, the Prophet, and his path is God's path.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا فالصراط مضاف للمتكلم وهو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وصراطه هو صراط الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r4.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ coordinates the clause with the pronoun in bihi and understands an omitted preposition; al-Hawfi says it is implicit, while Abu al-Baqaʾ rejects the parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r4.anchor: أن يكون في موضع جر عطفا على الضمير في به قاله الفراء، أي وصاكم به وبأن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r5.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads wa-hādhā ṣirāṭī instead of wa-an hādhā ṣirāṭī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r5.anchor:
وقرأ الأعمش:
وهذا صراطي وكذا في مصحف عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r6.claim: The demonstrative summarizes all preceding commands and may refer to Islam, the Qur'an, the surah's monotheism and prophetic proofs, or the unchanging commandments that follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r6.anchor: والإشارة بهذا إلى الإسلام أو القرآن أو ما ورد في هذه السورة لأنها كلها في التوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r7.claim: Following the path means acting on the whole of its prohibitions, permissions, commands, and restraints.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r7.anchor: فاعملوا بمقتضاه من تحريم وتحليل وأمر ونهي وإباحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the divergent paths as misguidances.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies the divergent paths as innovations, desires, and speculative doubts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r10.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies them as the livestock and crops people wrongly prohibited for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r10.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ما حرموا على أنفسهم من الأنعام والحرث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r11.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r11.claim: Another interpretation makes the paths religions of disbelief such as Judaism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p691/r11.anchor: وقيل: سبل الكفر كاليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية وما يجري مجراهم في الكفر والشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'this is My path' refers to the Prophet's law, fitting the following prohibition; other views refer to the commands and prohibitions in the two preceding verses or the surah's overall themes.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى شرعه عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r2.claim: Mujahid? No: the passage attributes this view to Muqatil, who takes the path as the commands and prohibitions in the two preceding verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r2.anchor: وعن مقاتل أنه إشارة إلى ما في الآيتين من الأمر والنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r3.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r3.claim: A third interpretation takes the path as the whole surah, most of which establishes monotheism and prophecy and explains the law.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : إلى ما ذكر في السورة فإن أكثرها في إثبات التوحيد والنبوة وبيان الشريعة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r4.claim: The particle in 'that you do not associate' is read with kasra by Hamza and al-Kisa'i, open and light by Ibn Amir and Yaqub, and open and doubled by the remaining readers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( إن ) بالكسر وابن عامر ويعقوب بالفتح والتخفيف والباقون به مشدد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r5.claim: Ibn Amir reads 'My path' with an open yāʾ; variants also read 'the path of your Lord' or 'the path of your Lord' in the singular address.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( صراطي ) بفتح الياء وقريء ( وهذا صراط ربكم وهذا صراط ربك )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r6.claim: The path is attributed to God by its institution and to the Prophet by his practice and invitation; it is straight, without crookedness, and must be followed in practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r6.anchor: وإضافة الصراط إلى الرب سبحانه من حيث الوضع وإليه عليه الصلاة والسلام من حيث السلوك والدعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prohibited 'paths' as misguidances; another report from him says they are divergent religions such as Judaism and Christianity.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r7.anchor: أي الضلالات كما أخرجه ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس وفي رواية عنه أنها الأديان المختلفة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the paths as innovations and doubts.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وعبد بن حميد وغيرهما عن مجاهد أنها البدع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r9.claim: The result clause after the prohibition deletes one of the two original taʾs; the causative bāʾ means the paths divide and scatter you, more forcefully than saying you yourselves divide.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r9.anchor: نصب في جواب النهي والأصل تتفرق فحذفت إحدى التائين والباء للتعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r10.claim: God's path is Islam, straight and unburdened; alternatively it is following revelation and proof. The Prophet's path is identical to God's, and attributing it to him first encourages following.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r10.anchor: أي سبيل الله تعالى الذي لا اعوجاج فيه ولا حرج لما هو دين الاسلام وقيل : هو اتباع الوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r11.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet drew one straight line as God's path, then side lines each bearing a devil who calls people to it, and recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطا بيده ثم قال : هذا سبيل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r12.claim: The closing reference reiterates the prohibition on following divergent paths and God's command to follow the straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56#2/r12.anchor: إشارة إلى إتباع السبل وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the closing aim as fearing God's punishment through performing commands and continuing to avoid prohibitions; following the encompassing straight path brings eternal salvation and lasting happiness.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r1.anchor: عقاب الله تعالى بالمثابرة على فعل ما أمر به والاستمرار على الكف عما نهى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r2.claim: Because the straight path gathers all duties, the repeated testament gives emphatic force to the command and closes with piety as protection from the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r2.anchor: ولما كان الصراط المستقيم هو الجامع للتكاليف وأمر سبحانه باتباعه ونهى عن اتباع غيره من الطرق ختم ذلك بالتقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.claim: A hasan report from Ibn Masud says whoever wishes to see the Prophet's testament bearing his seal should recite the verses beginning 'Say: come, I will recite' through 'that you may be mindful.'
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بخاتمه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.claim: Ubadah reports that the Prophet sought a pledge on these three verses: fulfillment earns God's reward; a shortcoming punished in this life is expiated, while a deferred matter is left to God's choice to punish or pardon.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث ثم تلاهن إلى آخرهن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says these decisive verses have never been abrogated in any scripture, are forbidden to all humanity, are the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise and abandoners to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.anchor: هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب وهن محرمات على بني آدم كلهم وهن أم الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.claim: The construction 'that you do not associate' may use a particle of explanation or a nominalizing particle; each choice raises syntactic and semantic objections.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r7.anchor: هذا و ( أن ) في قوله سبحانه ( أن لا تشركوا ) يحتمل أن تكون مفسرة وأن تكون مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.claim: If nominalizing, the phrase seems to name the forbidden act as association rather than refraining from it, and affirmative commands then follow a negative prohibition; treating 'do not' as a relative clause was a view attributed to Sibawayh but is rejected here.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r8.anchor: وظاهر أن المحرم هو الاشراك لا نفيه وأن الأوامر بعد معطوفة على ( لا تشركوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r9.claim: If explanatory, the following 'this is My path' does not syntactically explain the preceding negative command, and the affirmative commands do not explain a recitation of prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r9.anchor: وإن جعلت ( أن ) مفسرة و ( لا ) ناهية النواهي بيان لتلاوة المحرمات توجه إشكالان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari chooses the explanatory particle and includes later commands by understanding their opposites as implicit prohibitions; he connects 'this is My path' to 'follow it' with an omitted causal lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r10.anchor: واختار الزمخشري كونها مفسرة وعطف الأوامر لأنها معنى نواه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's solution makes the path clause a reason to follow the path, with the pronoun referring back to the previously mentioned straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r11.anchor: بأن قوله سبحانه ( وأن هذا صراطي ) ليس عطفا على ( أن لا تشركوا ) بل هو تعليل للاتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r1.claim: An objection says al-Zamakhshari's analysis conjoins the command to follow with the prohibition not to associate, yielding both wāw and fa; the reply is that wāw plus fa is common when an object intervenes.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r1.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون اتبعوه عطفا على ( لاتشركوا ) ويكون التقدير فاتبعوا صراطي لأنه مستقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r2.claim: Examples include 'your Lord magnify' and 'the mosques belong to God, so do not call anyone'; if the doubled conjunction is rejected, the fronted object may attach to an omitted verb such as 'hold fast,' followed by 'follow it.'
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r2.anchor: مثل ( وربك فكبر وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا ) فان أبيت الجمع البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers the second objection by treating affirmative commands as carrying an implicit prohibition of their opposites, such as not mistreating parents, shortchanging measures, abandoning justice, or breaking covenants.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r3.anchor: دل على أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها بمعنى أن الأوامر كأنها ذكرت وقصد لوازمها التي هي النهي عن الأضداد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says the commands may instead coordinate with 'I recite what God prohibited,' not with the prohibitions themselves, so the first clause introduces prohibitions and a second introduces commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r4.anchor: والثاني ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.claim: Alternatively, the explanatory particle may govern an omitted 'and what He commanded,' understood from the prohibition phrase; then positive and negative commands can both be explained and coordinated.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r5.anchor: ان تكون الأوامر معطوفة على المناهي داخلة تحت حكم التفسيرية ويصح هذا على تقدير محذوف تكون أن مفسرة له

ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r6.speaker: امرؤ القيس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r6.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line 'Do not perish in grief, and be composed' exemplifies coordinating an imperative with a prohibition; the source says this is not disputed, unlike coordination of declarative, interrogative, and imperative clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p58/r6.anchor: يجوز عطف الأمر على النهي والنهي على الأمر لقول أمريء القيس

ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says coordinating the path clause with 'come' is extremely unlikely; Abu Hayyan's account using an omitted phrase and interpreting the stated and omitted material together has merit.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p59/r1.anchor: العطف على ( تعالوا ) في غاية البعد ولا ينبغي الالتفات إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.claim: This straight path is the religion and way established by the commands in the preceding two verses; it is upright and true.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.anchor: {وأن هذا} أي: هذا الذي وصيتكم به في هاتين الآيتين {صراطي} طريقي وديني،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.claim: They read wa-in with kasra as a new sentence; the others read wa-an with fatha. Al-Farra says the meaning is I recite to you that this is my straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي "وإن" بكسر الألف على الاستئناف، وقرأ الآخرون: بفتح الألف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.claim: They read the nūn of wa-an with sukūn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب: بسكون النون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.claim: The forbidden paths are divergent routes such as Judaism, Christianity, and other religions, or alternatively desires and innovations; they cause people to veer and scatter from God's approved religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.anchor: {ولا تتبعوا السبل} أي: الطرق المختلفة التي عدا هذا الطريق، مثل اليهودية والنصرانية وسائر الملل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Prophet drew one line as God's path and side-lines as paths with a devil calling to each, then recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: خط لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطا ثم قال: "هذا سبيل الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r1.claim: The straight path refers to the surah as a whole: establishing monotheism and prophethood and explaining religious law.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r1.anchor: الإشارة فيه إلى ما ذكر في السورة فإنها بأسرها في إثبات التوحيد والنبوة وبيان الشريعة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read an with kasra as a new sentence; Ibn Amir and Yaqub use fatḥa with a light nūn, and the other readers double it with an implicit lām of purpose.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { ءان } بالكسر على الاستئناف، وابن عامر ويعقوب بالفتح والتخفيف. وقرأ الباقون بها مشددة

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads ṣirāṭī with a fatḥa on the yāʾ; other forms say this is my path or your Lord's path.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { صرطي } بفتح الياء، وقرىء «وهذا صراطي» «وهذا صراط ربكم»

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r4.claim: The prohibited paths are differing religions or desire-driven ways: evidence yields one course, while desires multiply with differing natures and customs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r4.anchor: الأديان المختلفة أو الطرق التابعة للهوى، فإن مقتضى الحجة واحد ومقتضى الهوى متعدد لاختلاف الطبائع والعادات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r5.claim: Fa-tafarraqa bikum means it divides or removes you from God's path, which is following revelation and proof; following the path protects from error and division.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:153/r5.anchor: فتفرقكم وتزيلكم. { عن سبيله } الذي هو اتباع الوحي واقتفاء البرهان. { ذلكم } الاتباع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r7.claim: Most readers use the opening waw with fath as a continuation; Ibn ʿAmir and Yaʿqub read it with kasra as the start of a new sentence.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r7.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالفتح , أي اتبعوه لذلك , وعلى قراءة ابن عامر ويعقوب بالكسر هو ابتداء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r8.claim: The straight path should be followed with full effort because it gathers people on truth and good, while paths branching from desire divide them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r8.anchor: أي بغاية جهدكم لأنه الجامع للعباد على الحق الذي فيه كل خير

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r9.claim: The author links this straight path to the earlier description of the Lord’s path and signs made clear for those who remember.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r9.anchor: وهذا كما مدحه سبحانه سابقا في قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.claim: The rulings are distributed across three verses, each ending with “He has charged you,” strengthening the instruction and inviting acceptance.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.anchor: وفصل ما هنا من الأحكام في ثلاث آيات , وختم كل آية لذلك بالوصية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.claim: The closing appeals progress from reason to remembrance to taqwa: reason calls for reflection, which leads to precaution against straying and ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.anchor: لأنه إذا كان العقل دعا إلى التذكير فحمل على التقوى

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.claim: Al-An‘am was revealed in Mecca as a whole except these three verses, which were revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سورة الأنعام نزلت بمكة جملة واحدة فهي مكية إلا ثلاث آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.claim: Al-An‘am descended all at once with ranks of angels stretching from the lowest heaven to earth; it was Meccan except 6:151–153.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.anchor:
عن شهر بن
حوشب قال: نزلت الأنعام جملة واحدة معها رجز من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.claim: The Prophet’s sealed testament is found in the three concluding commandments of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد التي عليها خاتما

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.claim: The Prophet sought a pledge to uphold these three verses: fulfillment earns reward, while shortcoming may be punished in life or left to God’s will in the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.claim: When asked for a written sheet bearing the Prophet’s seal, al-Rabi‘ recited these concluding verses from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.anchor: قال الربيع بن خيثم: أيسرك أن تلقى صحيفة من محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بخاتم

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.claim: Ka‘b says the first ten revealed verses of the Torah are these ten commandments at the end of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.anchor: عن كعب قال: أول ما نزل من التوراة عشر آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.claim: Ka‘b swears that the first verse in the Torah is the opening of these commandments from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.anchor: عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار قال: سمع كعب رجلا يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.claim: Asked for advice, al-Rabi‘ wrote down the three commandments at the end of al-An‘am and told the questioner to adhere to them.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.anchor: عن مزاحم بن زفر قال: قال رجل للربيع بن خيثم: أوصني

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.claim: At Mina, the Prophet invited an Arab tribe to affirm God’s oneness, recognize his messengership, and shelter and defend him; he recited these commandments, then 16:90. Mafruq praised their noble morals and Hani‘ approved his words.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادعوكم إلى شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r7.claim: There is one path of guidance leading to Paradise, while Satan devised divergent paths of error that lead to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r8.claim: The Prophet drew God’s straight path and side paths, each with a devil calling to it, then recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطا بيده ثم قال هذا سبيل الله مستقيما

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r9.claim: The Prophet drew a central path with two lines on each side, called them God’s path and Satan’s path, and recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فخط خطا هكذا أمامه

DURR-FULL:v3p386/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r1.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud describes the straight path as leading to Paradise, while side roads call people off it and lead to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا سأله ما الصراط المستقيم قال: تركنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v3p386/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ولا تتبعوا السبل} قال: الضلالات

DURR-FULL:v3p386/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r3.claim: The divergent paths are innovations and doubts.
DURR-FULL:v3p386/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولا تتبعوا السبل} قال: البدع والشبهات

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r4.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r4.claim: Nafi opens the eight listed added yāʾs except صراطي and ومحياي, which he quiesces; Warsh later reports فتح on the yāʾ of ومحياي.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r4.anchor: فقرأهن نافع بالفتح إلا قوله ﴿ صراطي ﴾ ﴿ ومحياي ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعاصم برواية أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai quiesce the listed yāʾs except they open ومحياي; Abu Bakr's Asim reading agrees.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى بإسكانهن إلا قوله ﴿ ومحياي ﴾ فإنهما فتحاها وكذلك عاصم فى رواية أبي بكر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r8.claim: Ibn Amir reads محياي, وجهي للذي, and صراطي with their yāʾs moving.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر / محياى / و ﴿ وجهي للذي ﴾ و / صرطى / محركات

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r10.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r10.claim: Abu Bakr says the surah has forty added yāʾs and only the eight listed here are disputed.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r10.anchor: قال أبو بكر فى هذه السورة أربعون ياء إضافة لم يختلف منها إلا فى هذه الياءات الثمان التى ذكرتهن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r1.claim: The demonstrative points to Islam, made mentally present through repeated Quranic revelation and the Messenger’s words; alternatively it points to the preceding laws and exhortations, present as if seen, like 3:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r1.anchor: والإشارة إلى الإسلام : أي وأن الإسلام صراطي ؛ فالإشارة إلى حاضر في أذهان المخاطبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r2.claim: The broad, established road means Islam, as the surah’s conclusion states; Islam brings well-being in this life and the next, so it is likened to a road leading to one’s goal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r2.anchor: والصراط : الطريق الجادة الواسعة ، وقد مر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r3.claim: Calling Islam straight presents it as a clear, visible road without bends, easier to travel and quicker to reach the destination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r3.anchor: فادعي أنه مستقيم ، أي لا اعوجاج فيه لأن الطريق المستقيم أيسر سلوكا على السائر وأسرع وصولا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r4.claim: The possessive ي in “My path” refers to God, supported by 42:52–53; shifting to first person signals this path’s immunity from error and grounds the command to follow it in being God’s path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r4.anchor: والياء المضاف إليها ( صراط ) تعود على الله ، كما بينه قوله : وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r5.claim: The possessive ي may instead refer to the Prophet who was commanded to speak; then the command to follow rests on his asserted clarity, since the path being his alone gives disbelievers no reason to follow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p172/r5.anchor: ويجوز عود الياء إلى النبيء المأمور بالقول ، إلا أن هذا يستدعي بناء التفريع بالأمر باتباعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r1.claim: The participle مستقيم is circumstantial from the demonstrative: deixis makes the path mentally present as a whole, so it appears perceptible; such circumstantial use after demonstratives is common, as in 11:72.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r1.anchor: حال من اسم الإشارة ، وحسن وقوعه حالا أن الإشارة بنيت على ادعاء أنه مشاهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r2.claim: Sبل means roads; contrast with the straight path supplies an omitted description, divergent, crooked side paths called بنيات الطريق, which branch off the main road and lead only to homes or pastures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r2.anchor: والسبل : الطرق ، ووقوعها هنا في مقابلة الصراط المستقيم يدل على صفة محذوفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r3.claim: The paths separate travelers from God's main way; this is not because سبيل means an unconnected narrow track, since سبيل can be synonymous with صراط, as in 12:108.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r3.anchor: وليس ذلك لأن السبيل اسم للطريق الضيقة غير الموصلة ، فإن السبيل يرادف الصراط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r4.claim: The ب in بكم marks accompaniment: the paths and travelers diverge together; this figurative accompaniment functions like a causative hamza, as in ذهبت بزيد meaning أذهبته.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r4.anchor: والباء في قوله : { بكم } للمصاحبة : أي فتتفرق السبل مصاحبة لكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r5.claim: The pronoun in سبيله refers to God by context; if صراطي also refers to God, سبيله shifts person as iltifāt from the first-person form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r5.anchor: والضمير المضاف إليه في : { سبيله } يعود إلى الله تعالى بقرينة المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet drew one line as God's path and side lines with a devil calling from each, then recited this verse; the listed collections transmit the report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود ، قال : خط لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما خطا ثم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r7.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet marked a middle path and lines to its right and left, identified the middle as God's path, and recited the verse; Ibn Ashur says the first report's plural counts both sides together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p173/r7.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : ( كنا عند النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم فخط خطا وخط خطين عن يمينه

TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.claim: Truth is one and unified, whereas falsehood is scattered and divisive; therefore true propositions cohere and support one another rather than contradicting one another.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.anchor: فقد جعل الحق واحدا لا تفرق فيه ولا تشتت

MUSNAD-AHMAD:15277/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:15277/r1.speaker: جابر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:15277/r1.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet drew a central line as God's path and lines to either side as Satan's paths, then recited 6:153.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:15277/r1.anchor: عن جابر، قال: كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فخط خطا هكذا أمامه، فقال: " هذا سبيل الله

TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that anyone wishing to see the page bearing Muḥammad's seal should recite the commandments from 6:151 through 6:153; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى الصَّحِيفَةِ الَّتِي عَلَيْهَا خَاتَمُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْيَقْرَأْ هَذِهِ الآيَاتِ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r1.claim: Qasas uses the command usluk for Moses’ hand because the story repeatedly has people traverse places and paths, while Naml omits the travel episodes and starts with Moses speaking to his family at the fire.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r1.anchor: ذلك لأنه تردد سلوكُ الأمكنةِ والسبل في قصة موسى في القصص، بخلاف ما ورد في النمل.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r2.claim: The Qasas narrative recounts the chest traveling to Pharaoh’s palace, the sister tracking Moses, Moses’ flight to Midian, his route to the righteous man, and his return journey; this makes its language of traversing apt.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r2.anchor: فقد ورد فيها، أي: في سورة القصص سلوك الصندوق بموسى، وهو مُلقى في اليمّ إلى قصر فرعون، وسلوك أخته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r3.claim: The verb dakhal and its derivatives occur five times in Naml but not in Qasas, another reason the author gives for using adkhil in Naml and usluk in Qasas.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r3.anchor: الفعل (دخل) ومشتقاته تكرر خمس مرات في النمل في حين، لم يرد هذا الفعل ولا شيء من مشتقاته في القصص،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r4.claim: Idkhāl is more specific than sulūk: sulūk can mean entering, but it can also mean traveling along a road or through a place.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p111/r4.anchor: إن الإدخال أخص من السَّلْك أو السلوك اللذين هما مصدر الفعل سلك، لأن السَّلْك أو السلوك، قد يكون إدخالاً وغير إدخال

NASHR:v2p266/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p266/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
NASHR:v2p266/r7.claim: Ibn Amir opens the yāʾ of صراطي مستقيما.

NASHR:v2p265#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p265#2/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p265#2/r10.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read the hamza of وأن هذا with kasra; the others use fatha, with Yaqub and Ibn Amir lightening the nūn and the rest doubling it.
NASHR:v2p265#2/r10.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بكسر الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها إلا أن يعقوب وابن عامر خففا النون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r1.claim: God sent messengers as bearers of good news and warnings so people would have no plea against Him after the messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r1.anchor: والحمد لله الذي أرسل رسله {مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r2.claim: God sealed the messengers with the unlettered Arab Meccan Prophet, a guide to the clearest paths, sent to all humans and jinn until the Hour.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r2.anchor: وختمهم بالنبي الأمي العربي المكي الهادي لأوضح السبل، أرسله إلى جميع خلقه من الإنس والجن، من لدن بعثته إلى قيام الساعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r3.claim: Everyone reached by the Qur’an—Arab or non-Arab, human or jinn, of every complexion—is warned by it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r3.anchor: فمن بلغه هذا القرآن من عرب وعجم، وأسود وأحمر، وإنس وجان، فهو نذير له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r4.claim: Whoever among those reached disbelieves in the Qur’an has Hell as his appointed destination, as God explicitly states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r4.anchor: فمن كفر بالقرآن ممن ذكرنا (1) فالنار موعده، بنص الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said that he was sent to the red and the black.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r5.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بعثت إلى الأحمر والأسود"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses the Prophet’s “red and black” as humans and jinn.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r7.claim: The Qur’an is a revelation from the Wise, Praiseworthy God that no falsehood can approach from before or behind.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r7.anchor: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r8.claim: God calls people to understand and ponder the Qur’an, as shown by several commands to reflect on it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r8.anchor: وقد أعلمهم فيه عن الله تعالى أنه ندبهم إلى تفهمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r9.claim: Scholars must disclose and interpret God’s words, seek the knowledge in its proper sources, and learn and teach it; concealing it is condemned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5#2/r9.anchor: فالواجب على العلماء الكشف عن معاني كلام الله، وتفسير ذلك، وطلبه من مظانه، وتعلم ذلك وتعليمه

BURHAN:v4p12/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p12/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p12/r1.claim: Truth’s path is singular because it is one, while falsehood’s paths are numerous; likewise the true religion is light and error consists of many darknesses.
BURHAN:v4p12/r1.anchor: والجواب في ذلك كله أن طريق الحق واحد وأما الباطل فطرقه متشعبة متعددة ولما كانت الظلم بمنزلة طريق الباطل والنور بمنزلة طريق الجنة

BURHAN:v4p12/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p12/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p12/r2.claim: God is named the singular guardian of believers, whereas the guardians of unbelievers are plural because they are many; darknesses are plural for the many divergent paths of error, and light is singular for true religion.
BURHAN:v4p12/r2.anchor: لأنه الواحد الأحد وجمع أولياء الكفار لتعددهم وجمع الظلمات وهي طرق الضلال والغى لكثرتها

ITQAN:v3p6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the final three verses of al-An'am are clear, beginning with قل تعالوا.
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وغيره عن ابن عباس قال

ITQAN:v3p6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas locates three clear verses at قل تعالوا and three more at وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه.
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v2p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p564/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p564/r1.claim: Truth is expressed as one path and falsehood as many paths because truth is one and false routes branch; light is likewise singular and darkness plural. The same pattern appears in the singular ally of believers and plural allies of disbelievers.
ITQAN:v2p564/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك إفراد النور وجمع الظلمات وإفراد سبيل الحق

ITQAN:v2p564/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p564/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p564/r2.claim: Hell is singular wherever it occurs, while Paradise is singular or plural: gardens differ in kind, Hell is one substance, and mercy suits plurality while punishment suits singularity.
ITQAN:v2p564/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك إفراد النار حيث وقعت والجنة وقعت مجموعة ومفردة لأن الجنان مختلفة الأنواع فحسن جمعها والنار مادة واحدة

ITQAN:v2p564/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p564/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p564/r5.claim: The word الألباب occurs only in plural because its singular form is phonologically heavy.
ITQAN:v2p564/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك الألباب لم يقع إلا مجموعا لأن مفرده ثقيل لفظا

ITQAN:v2p564/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p564/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p564/r6.claim: East and west occur in singular for direction, dual for the summer and winter rising and setting points, and plural for the many seasonal points.
ITQAN:v2p564/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك مجيء المشرق والمغرب بالإفراد والتثنية والجمع فحيث أفردا فاعتبارا للجهة وحيث ثنيا فاعتبارا لمشرق الصيف والشتاء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r1.claim: Several independent similes in one line do not alter one another or combine into a new image; their merit comes from concise, artful arrangement.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r1.anchor: لا أن حقائق التشبيهات تتغير بهذا الجمع أو أن الصور تتداخل وتتركب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r2.claim: Bashshār’s simile is composite: it presents the whole battlefield scene of dark dust and flashing, rising and falling swords as one image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r2.anchor: أن يريك الهيئة التى ترى عليها النقع المظلم والسيوف في أثنائه تبرق وتومض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r3.claim: Ruʾba’s skin comparison concerns the combined appearance of black and white markings, not each color separately.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r3.anchor: ليس القصد فيه أن يريك كل لون على الانفراد وإنما القصد أن يرى الشبه من اجتماع اللونين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r4.claim: Al-Buḥturī compares the combined look of a horse’s white fetlocks against a dark cloud to lightning, not whiteness alone.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r4.anchor: لا يريد به تشبيه بياض الحجول على الانفراد بالبرق بل المقصود الهيئة الخاصة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r5.claim: In Bashshār’s line, وأسيافنا remains attached to the source phrase as one unit, preventing the simile from being split into separate comparisons.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r5.anchor: وأسيافنا في حكم الصلة للمصدر وجار مجرى الأسم الواحد لئلا يقع في التشبيه تفريق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r6.claim: The conjunction means مع in examples such as فإني وقيار and كل رجل وضيعته, so the coordinated material does not form a second sentence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r6.anchor: لأن الواو فيها بمعنى مع كقوله فإني وقيار بها لغريب وقوله كل رجل وضيعته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r7.claim: The example لو تركت الناقة وفصيلها لرضعها cannot be divided into two conditional sentences, supporting the connected construction.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p169/r7.anchor: لو تركت الناقة وفصيلها لرضعها لا يكون بمنزلة أن تقول لو تركت الناقة ولو ترك فصيلها

DAMGHANI:v1p278/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r1.claim: The straight path in 6:153 means God’s religion; 6:126 similarly calls it the straight path of the Lord.
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r1.anchor: وقال تعالى فى سورة الأنعام وان هذا صراطى مستقيما يعنى دينى وقوله تعالى فيها وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما يعنى دين ربك مستقيما
